findings.reason: the author must either keep a per-source semantic bridge for escalated sources or state the intended behaviour change and which prompt block replaces `semantic_match_matrix`.
findings.text: §8 retires the `compute_semantic_matches` call that is the sole producer of the per-source `semantic_match_matrix` (consumed at `imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:1058` and `:1245` to fill the assign/map prompts' `match_matrix_ctx`), and presents `fetch_wiki_context` (`imas_codex/ids/tools.py:638`) and `fetch_code_context` (`imas_codex/ids/tools.py:681`) as its replacement; but those two are physics-domain-filtered graph queries with no embedding, already called separately at `imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:637,647` to fill the facility-level context block, so an escalated source loses its per-source wiki/code semantic bridge and the plan does not name what fills that prompt slot

findings.reason: `write_candidates` deletes and rewrites every edge for the source, so a targeted mark genuinely cannot use it and cannot be a thin wrapper; only the one-line justification is missing from the plan text.
findings.text: §8 adds `select_candidate(source_id, path)` to mark the reasoning model's pick of a shortlist path beside the existing `write_candidates`, and the two overlap on the `r.route` edge flag with no statement of why the writer cannot be extended or reused

findings.reason: both are terminal claim-loop helpers delegating to `imas_codex/discovery/base/claims.py`, so they do not fork the store owner; the plan only needs to scope its "one owner" claim to the count reader rather than to every candidate-state query.
findings.text: §8 states that after moving `count_candidates_by_route` into `graph_ops.py`, "every candidate-state query has one owner", but `has_pending_candidate_work` (`imas_codex/ids/workers.py:403`) and the candidate claim predicate (`imas_codex/ids/workers.py:326`, `n.candidate_route IS NULL`) both read candidate state in `workers.py`, and §8 neither moves them nor accounts for them

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `imas_codex/ids/candidates.py` hides embedding, arm merge, decisions transport and thresholding behind `retrieve_candidates`/`route_ids`/`judge_candidates`/`route`, and §8 keeps the MAPPING_CANDIDATE store behind those callers rather than wrapping them.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the plan names `imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py` as the single owner, moves `count_candidates_by_route` into it, deletes `count_sources_by_mapping_status` and `create_signal_source`, and reconciles the three `MAPS_TO_IMAS` writers (`models.py:580`, `graph_ops.py:367`, `mapping.py:2008`) with the one delete site (`cli/map.py:661`) — each verified by the node's own census commands.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §8 retires two CLI options (`--skip-metadata`, `--skip-errors`) and three public functions (`compute_semantic_matches`, `create_signal_source`, `count_sources_by_mapping_status`) while adding two store functions, so no listed family grows unaccounted in the section's own text.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites `compute_semantic_matches` as replaced by `fetch_wiki_context`/`fetch_code_context`, but those are domain-filtered graph queries, not the per-source semantic bridge that fills the prompt's `semantic_match_matrix` slot.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §8 adds `select_candidate` beside `write_candidates` without saying why the existing writer cannot mark the pick.
